3	/// Clip ▸ Remove Silences… — road map 2 phase 3a's dialog: five controls
4	/// (Judge by, the threshold, Longer than, Keep at ends, In), a live count of
5	/// what they would cut, the same spans washed onto the timeline behind the
6	/// sheet, and one `ripple_delete_ranges` op when Remove is pressed.
7	///
8	/// **Everything it measures is read once, in `init`.** `SilenceDetector.Input`
9	/// is the snapshot, the composition plan, the selection and every peaks file
10	/// the timeline's media has, taken off the document in one pass. That is safe
11	/// because the document cannot change under an open sheet — every editor
12	/// action validates false while one is attached
13	/// (`EditorViewController.validateUserInterfaceItem`) — and it is what lets
14	/// `refresh()` run SYNCHRONOUSLY on every slider tick: after the first read
15	/// a detection is arithmetic over a few thousand floats already in memory,
16	/// with no file, no FFI and no queue in it. A background hop would buy
17	/// nothing and would make the commit off-event, which drags
18	/// `performGroupedEdit` and a staleness check in behind it.
19	///
20	/// The one thing that CAN change under the sheet is the peaks cache: it is
21	/// written by the fire-and-forget task `ProjectDocument.generateCaches()`
22	/// starts, so a project opened seconds ago may still be analysing. Media in
23	/// that state is never proposed for removal (the detector treats a missing
24	/// cache as "never quiet", because proposing to delete a whole clip because
25	/// its waveform has not landed is the one failure this feature must not
26	/// have), the readout says so, and `.mediaCacheDidChange` re-reads the input
27	/// and recomputes as each file lands — the same notification `MediaPane` and
28	/// `TimelineView` already watch.

285	    /// The second line, when there is something the count alone would hide.
286	    /// All three readings below can come out as "0 cuts" and none of them
287	    /// means "there is no dead air here", which is why they are spelled out
288	    /// — and they are JOINED rather than answered first-match, because a
289	    /// project can easily be two of them at once.
290	    private func noteText() -> String {
291	        var notes: [String] = []
292	        if outcome.clips.isEmpty {
293	            notes.append(
294	                outcome.scope == .selected
295	                    ? "Nothing the selected clips play is audible in the mix, so nothing "
296	                        + "was analysed."
297	                    : "Nothing in this timeline is audible, so nothing was analysed.")
298	        } else if !outcome.pendingMedia.isEmpty {
299	            // Named rather than counted: which file is still being analysed
300	            // is what tells the user whether to wait or to go ahead, and the
301	            // sheet re-runs by itself the moment one lands.
302	            let names = outcome.pendingMedia.compactMap { input.snapshot.media($0)?.name }
303	            let listed = names.isEmpty
304	                ? (outcome.pendingMedia.count == 1
305	                    ? "one file" : "\(outcome.pendingMedia.count) files")
306	                : names.joined(separator: ", ")
307	            // The promise is the LEVEL rule's: a media with no peaks is never
308	            // quiet there. In voice mode the model has landed and spans
309	            // inside the file are proposed — only a clip it found no voice in
310	            // waits for the waveform (the reader review, road map 4 §8, R3·1).
311	            notes.append(
312	                outcome.mode == .level
313	                    ? "The waveform is still being analysed for \(listed). "
314	                        + promise(about: outcome.pendingMedia)
315	                    : "The waveform is still being analysed for \(listed). "
316	                        + waveformPromise())
317	        }
318	        if !input.voiceAvailable {
319	            notes.append(
320	                "The voice model could not be used, so quiet is judged by level.")
321	        }
322	        if !outcome.voicePending.isEmpty {
323	            let names = outcome.voicePending.compactMap { input.snapshot.media($0)?.name }
324	            let listed = names.isEmpty
325	                ? (outcome.voicePending.count == 1
326	                    ? "one file" : "\(outcome.voicePending.count) files")
327	                : names.joined(separator: ", ")
328	            notes.append(
329	                "Speech is still being analysed for \(listed). "
330	                    + promise(about: outcome.voicePending))
331	        }
332	        // Named by CLIP (#107): two clips of one file can be judged
333	        // differently, so the file's name alone would not say which.
334	        let byLevel = SilenceDetector.VoiceAnswer.labels(
335	            outcome.answers.filter { $0.judgedByLevel }, in: input.snapshot)
336	        if byLevel.count == 1 {
337	            notes.append("\(byLevel[0]) holds no voice and is judged by level.")
338	        } else if byLevel.count > 1 {
339	            notes.append(
340	                "\(byLevel.count) clips hold no voice and are judged by level: "
341	                    + byLevel.joined(separator: ", ") + ".")
342	        }
343	        if !outcome.protectedNests.isEmpty {
344	            // The detector will not propose a span that reaches into a nest
345	            // (`SilenceDetector`'s doc says why), so a nested screencast
346	            // finds fewer cuts than its waveform looks like it holds. Left
347	            // unsaid, that reads as "there is no dead air here".
348	            let count = outcome.protectedNests.count
349	            let subject = count == 1 ? "a nest" : "\(count) nests"
350	            notes.append(
351	                "Quiet inside \(subject) is left alone: a nest plays from its first frame, "
352	                    + "so cutting into one would strand the rest of it. Open the nest (⌘↓) "
353	                    + "and remove its silences there to take the dead air out.")
354	        }
355	        return notes.joined(separator: " ")
356	    }

358	    /// The "nothing inside is proposed" line, made about what the ANSWER
359	    /// shows rather than about the mode: the gain FLOOR is asked before
360	    /// either cache (`SilenceDetector.isQuiet`), so a clip the mix has turned
361	    /// down, faded, ducked or muted is quiet with nothing on disk at all and
362	    /// its spans are in the readout above this line (the reader review, road
363	    /// map 4 §8, finding 2). The tool's twin says the same in
364	    /// `AgentServer+Silence`. Since #107 it names the clips it is about.
365	    private func promise(about pending: [UInt32]) -> String {
366	        let labels = SilenceDetector.VoiceAnswer.labels(
367	            outcome.mixAnswers(inside: Set(pending)), in: input.snapshot)
368	        guard !labels.isEmpty else { return "Nothing inside is proposed for removal yet." }
369	        return "What is proposed inside \(labels.joined(separator: ", ")) is quiet in the MIX "
370	            + "— turned down, faded or ducked — which neither cache can change."
371	    }

373	    /// The VOICE-mode waveform line's own promise, which is narrower than
374	    /// `promise(about:)` above and cannot borrow it (the reader review's
375	    /// second sceptic pass, road map 4 §8). In voice mode the model has
376	    /// landed for most of what is on screen, so a media whose waveform is
377	    /// late still has spans proposed inside it BY THE MODEL — `promise` would
378	    /// then answer "quiet in the MIX", which is false about a clip nothing
379	    /// has turned down. What is true is an EXCEPTION, named by clip (#107):
380	    /// the clips of those media whose own answer is proposed while the cache
381	    /// their quiet test reads is missing (`Outcome.mixAnswers`) — a clip that
382	    /// holds no voice waiting on this waveform, or one whose speech cache has
383	    /// not landed either (`SilenceDetector.detect` returns on a missing
384	    /// speech cache BEFORE the by-level test, so such a clip is waiting on
385	    /// its speech). Only the FLOOR can propose inside a waiting clip, so what
386	    /// it names is what the mix made quiet, and a clip of the same file the
387	    /// mix left alone is not named.
388	    private func waveformPromise() -> String {
389	        let plain = "Anything inside it that holds no voice is left alone until it lands"
390	        let labels = SilenceDetector.VoiceAnswer.labels(
391	            outcome.mixAnswers(inside: Set(outcome.pendingMedia)), in: input.snapshot)
392	        guard !labels.isEmpty else { return plain + "." }
393	        return plain + ", except where the mix already turns "
394	            + labels.joined(separator: ", ") + " down far enough to be quiet."
395	    }

645	/// The cached Silero VAD probabilities — `cache/speech/<id>.bin` — and how to
646	/// ask them about a window, `MediaPeaks`' shape for the voice cache.
647	///
648	/// One 32-bit float per 512-sample chunk at 16 kHz (`SileroVAD.chunkSamples`
649	/// / `SileroVAD.sampleRate`), which is `chunkTicks` ticks of SOURCE time —
650	/// exactly 19,200, and written as the division rather than as the number for
651	/// the same reason `MediaPeaks.bucketTicks` is. `MediaPeaks.window` already
652	/// generalises the project-time → bucket-index arithmetic over the bucket
653	/// size, and `MediaPeaks.peak` takes the max over it on any grid, so this
654	/// file adds only the chunk grid, its loader and the question
655	/// `SilenceDetector`'s voice test asks.
656	enum MediaSpeech {
657	
658	    /// One probability's worth of source time, in ticks. Written as the
659	    /// division: `SileroVAD.sampleRate` and `SileroVAD.chunkSamples` each
660	    /// have exactly one home.
661	    static var chunkTicks: Ticks {
662	        ReelTime.perSecond * Ticks(SileroVAD.chunkSamples) / Ticks(SileroVAD.sampleRate)
663	    }
664	
665	    /// How many probabilities a file of `duration` produces — `writeSpeech`'s
666	    /// output length, so a caller can size the zero-filled buffer before any
667	    /// chunk lands.
668	    static func chunkCount(duration: Ticks) -> Int {
669	        max(1, Int((Double(duration) / Double(chunkTicks)).rounded(.up)))
670	    }
671	
672	    /// One media's cached probabilities read at most once, however many
673	    /// segments cite it — a `MediaCacheLoader` over `loadSpeech` instead of
674	    /// `loadPeaks`.
675	    static func loader(cacheDirectory: URL?) -> MediaCacheLoader<[Float]> {
676	        MediaCacheLoader(cacheDirectory: cacheDirectory) {
677	            MediaImporter.loadSpeech(for: $0, in: $1)
678	        }
679	    }

682	    /// `[from, to)` of `segment` covers, or 0 when it falls outside the
683	    /// window the cache was built from: `MediaPeaks.peak` asked on the chunk
684	    /// grid.
685	    static func speechMax(
686	        _ p: [Float], over segment: PlanSegment, from: Ticks, to: Ticks, reversedPivot: Ticks?
687	    ) -> Float {
688	        MediaPeaks.peak(
689	            p, over: segment, from: from, to: to, reversedPivot: reversedPivot,

697	    /// The three numbers, read in the sheet's own units and refused by name.
698	    ///
699	    /// The sheet clamps its controls to `Settings`' published ranges because
700	    /// a slider must land somewhere; a tool does not, and clamping an
701	    /// argument silently would report a detection the caller did not ask
702	    /// for. What is refused here is what is not a level or not a length at
703	    /// all — everything else is passed through and named back in the result,
704	    /// so a caller reading `threshold_db` sees what actually ran.
705	    private func silenceSettings(
706	        _ a: [String: Any], scope: SilenceDetector.Scope, voiceAvailable: Bool
707	    ) throws -> (SilenceDetector.Settings, String?) {
708	        var settings = SilenceDetector.Settings(scope: scope)
709	        var note: String?
710	        if let modeString = try stringArg(a, "mode") {
711	            guard let mode = SilenceDetector.Mode(rawValue: modeString) else {
712	                throw ToolError(
713	                    message: "mode must be \"voice\" or \"level\".")
714	            }
715	            if mode == .voice, !voiceAvailable {
716	                throw ToolError(
717	                    message: "The voice model could not be used; call with mode: \"level\".")
718	            }
719	            settings.mode = mode
720	        } else if !voiceAvailable {
721	            settings.mode = .level
722	            note = "The voice model could not be used, so quiet is judged by level."
723	        }
724	        if let voiceConfidence = try doubleArg(a, "voice_confidence") {
725	            guard settings.mode == .voice else {
726	                throw ToolError(
727	                    message: "voice_confidence only applies in mode: \"voice\".")
728	            }
729	            guard voiceConfidence.isFinite,
730	                SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.contains(voiceConfidence)
731	            else {
732	                throw ToolError(
733	                    message: "voice_confidence must be a number in "
734	                        + "\(SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.lowerBound)…"
735	                        + "\(SilenceDetector.Settings.voiceConfidenceRange.upperBound).")
736	            }
737	            settings.voiceConfidence = voiceConfidence
738	        }
739	        if let thresholdDB = try doubleArg(a, "threshold_db") {
740	            // Above full scale every bucket of every recording counts as
741	            // quiet and the whole timeline comes back as one candidate.
742	            // Peaks are unclamped and a hot source really does read over
743	            // 1.0, so this is a caller's mistake — a level in gain, or a
744	            // sign forgotten — rather than an impossible number.
745	            guard thresholdDB.isFinite, thresholdDB <= 0 else {
746	                throw ToolError(
747	                    message: "threshold_db must be a level at or below 0 dBFS (full scale); "
748	                        + "the default is \(SilenceDetector.Settings.defaultThresholdDB).")
749	            }
750	            settings.thresholdDB = thresholdDB
751	        }
752	        // Both lengths are DURATIONS, and a duration is not a position: they
753	        // are read as given, by the whole-number reader, and are NOT snapped
754	        // to the frame grid. The sheet's own two fields are not snapped
755	        // either (`SilenceSheetController.silenceSettings`'
756	        // `ReelTime.ticks(seconds:)`) and this tool exists to mirror it; the
757	        // frame rule stays where it belongs, on the span BOUNDS `refine`
758	        // produces, so no sub-frame time reaches an op from here. Going
759	        // through `optionalTimeArg` cost that mirror at the DEFAULT rate:
760	        // at 30 fps it ran `padding: 30000` — the sheet's own 0.05 s — as
761	        // 40000, ran `min_length: 45000` as 40000, and dropped
762	        // `padding: 9999` to 0, cutting the material the caller asked to
763	        // keep (the reader review, road map 4 §8, R1·1).
764	        //
765	        // What `optionalTimeArg` DID carry and a duration still needs is its
766	        // CEILING: `refine` adds the padding to a run's start, and a padding
767	        // at `Int64.max` overflowed and killed the app rather than answering
768	        // (the reader review, road map 4 §8, finding 1). The bound is
769	        // `snappedTick`'s own ±9.0e15, refused in a sentence naming the
770	        // argument. The sheet's two fields cannot reach it — they clamp to
771	        // `minLengthRange` and `paddingRange` — so the guard belongs here,
772	        // on the one caller that is not a slider.
773	        if let minLength = try intArg(a, "min_length") {
774	            guard minLength >= 0, minLength <= Self.durationCeiling else {
775	                throw ToolError(
776	                    message: "min_length must be a length in ticks (600000 per second) from 0 "
777	                        + "to \(Self.durationCeiling).")
778	            }
779	            settings.minLength = Ticks(minLength)
780	        }
781	        if let padding = try intArg(a, "padding") {
782	            guard padding >= 0, padding <= Self.durationCeiling else {
783	                throw ToolError(
784	                    message: "padding must be a length in ticks (600000 per second) from 0 "
785	                        + "to \(Self.durationCeiling).")
786	            }
787	            settings.padding = Ticks(padding)
788	        }
789	        return (settings, note)
790	    }

14	    /// `uh-huh` as one token. Another source's fillers (TR-7) are added by
15	    /// that source's own entry.

156	    /// The document's snapshot, scope and transcript cache, read once.
157	    ///
158	    /// Named clips are the scope (`.selected`); with none named, the
159	    /// selection when `Transcriber.jobs` accepts any of it, else every clip.
160	    /// The EDITED project, as `SilenceDetector.read` takes it: with a nest
161	    /// open the ranges are the nest's, in the nest's own time.
162	    static func read(from document: ProjectDocument, clips named: [UInt32]?) -> Input {
163	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
164	        let urls = document.mediaURLs()
165	        let maps = document.editedProject.sourceMap
166	        let scope: Scope
167	        let chosen: [ClipSnapshot]
168	        if let named {
169	            let ids = Set(named)
170	            chosen = snapshot.clips.filter { ids.contains($0.id) }
171	            scope = .selected
172	        } else {
173	            let selected = snapshot.clips.filter { document.selection.contains($0.id) }
174	            if !Transcriber.jobs(for: selected, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: maps).jobs.isEmpty {
175	                chosen = selected
176	                scope = .selected
177	            } else {
178	                chosen = snapshot.clips
179	                scope = .all
180	            }
181	        }
182	        let (kept, locked) = onUnlockedTracks(chosen, in: snapshot)
183	        let (jobs, problems) = Transcriber.jobs(for: kept, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: maps)
184	        let cacheDirectory = document.cacheDirectory
185	
186	        var clips: [ClipWords] = []
187	        var needs: Set<UInt32> = []
188	        var scopeFiles: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File?] = [:]
189	        for job in jobs {
190	            if scopeFiles[job.media] == nil {
191	                scopeFiles[job.media] = .some(
192	                    cacheDirectory.flatMap { cache in
193	                        snapshot.media(job.media).flatMap {
194	                            fillersFile(for: $0, url: job.source, in: cache)
195	                        }
196	                    })
197	            }
198	            if let file = scopeFiles[job.media] ?? nil {
199	                clips.append(ClipWords(job: job, file: file))
200	            } else {
201	                needs.insert(job.media)
202	            }
203	        }
204	
205	        var neighbours: [ClipWords] = []
206	        if let cacheDirectory {
207	            let unlocked = onUnlockedTracks(snapshot.clips, in: snapshot).kept
208	            var files: [UInt32: MediaTranscript.File?] = [:]
209	            let found = Transcriber.jobs(for: unlocked, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: maps)
210	            for job in found.jobs {
211	                if files[job.media] == nil {
212	                    files[job.media] = .some(
213	                        snapshot.media(job.media).flatMap {
214	                            transcriptFile(
215	                                for: $0, url: job.source, in: cacheDirectory, use: .captions)
216	                        })
217	                }
218	                if let file = files[job.media] ?? nil {
219	                    neighbours.append(ClipWords(job: job, file: file))
220	                }
221	            }
222	        }
223	        return Input(
224	            fps: snapshot.canvas.fps, scope: scope, clips: clips, needsTranscript: needs.sorted(),
225	            skipped: named == nil ? [] : problems, locked: locked, neighbours: neighbours,
226	            nests: SilenceDetector.nestExtents(in: snapshot),
227	            walls: SilenceDetector.overlapWalls(snapshot))
228	    }

232	    static func fillersFile(
233	        for media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, in cacheDir: URL

238	    /// A media's cached transcript when the file as it is NOW stamps the
239	    /// marker's source, the file reads, and the marker serves `use` for the
240	    /// request the file records; else nil.
241	    static func transcriptFile(
242	        for media: MediaSnapshot, url: URL, in cacheDir: URL, use: TranscriptUse
243	    ) -> MediaTranscript.File? {
244	        guard let stamp = MediaImporter.CacheStamp.stamp(for: media, url: url),
245	            let file = MediaTranscript.read(for: media.id, in: cacheDir),
246	            let marker = MediaTranscript.readStamp(for: media.id, in: cacheDir),
247	            marker.serves(TranscriptStamp(source: stamp, options: file.header.requested), for: use)
248	        else { return nil }
249	        return file
250	    }

252	    /// The clips not on a locked track, and the ids of those that are,
253	    /// sorted. A track the snapshot cannot find counts as unlocked, as the
254	    /// nest walls read it.
255	    static func onUnlockedTracks(
256	        _ clips: [ClipSnapshot], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot
257	    ) -> (kept: [ClipSnapshot], locked: [UInt32]) {
258	        var kept: [ClipSnapshot] = []
259	        var locked: [UInt32] = []
260	        for clip in clips {
261	            if snapshot.track(clip.track)?.locked == true {
262	                locked.append(clip.id)
263	            } else {
264	                kept.append(clip)
265	            }
266	        }
267	        return (kept, locked.sorted())
268	    }

270	    // MARK: - The arithmetic
271	
272	    /// One word of a clip's window, in source ticks.
273	    private struct Timed {
274	        let text: String
275	        let start: Ticks
276	        let end: Ticks
277	        let filler: Bool
278	    }
279	
280	    /// The clip's words in source ticks: those whose start is in its window
281	    /// (R6-10), sorted by start then end.
282	    private static func timed(_ file: MediaTranscript.File, in job: Transcriber.Job) -> [Timed] {
283	        let windowEnd = job.sourceIn + job.sourceLength
284	        var out: [Timed] = []
285	        for word in file.words {
286	            let start = MediaTranscript.sourceTicks(milliseconds: word.start)
287	            guard start >= job.sourceIn, start < windowEnd else { continue }
288	            out.append(
289	                Timed(
290	                    text: word.text, start: start,
291	                    end: MediaTranscript.sourceTicks(milliseconds: max(word.start, word.end)),
292	                    filler: FillerWords.isFiller(word.text)))
293	        }
294	        return out.sorted { ($0.start, $0.end) < ($1.start, $1.end) }
295	    }
296	
297	    /// Every maximal run of consecutive fillers in the clip's word order,
298	    /// with the non-filler words that bound it (TR-9).
299	    static func runs(of file: MediaTranscript.File, in job: Transcriber.Job) -> [Run] {
300	        let words = timed(file, in: job)
301	        let windowEnd = job.sourceIn + job.sourceLength
302	        // The latest non-filler end before each index, and the earliest
303	        // non-filler start after it.
304	        var before = [Ticks](repeating: job.sourceIn, count: words.count + 1)
305	        for (index, word) in words.enumerated() {
306	            before[index + 1] = word.filler ? before[index] : max(before[index], word.end)
307	        }
308	        var after = [Ticks](repeating: windowEnd, count: words.count + 1)
309	        for index in stride(from: words.count - 1, through: 0, by: -1) {
310	            let word = words[index]
311	            after[index] = word.filler ? after[index + 1] : min(after[index + 1], word.start)
312	        }
313	        var runs: [Run] = []
314	        var open: [Int] = []
315	        func close() {
316	            guard let first = open.first, let last = open.last else { return }
317	            runs.append(
318	                Run(
319	                    words: open.map { words[$0].text },
320	                    source: SilenceDetector.Span(
321	                        start: words[first].start, end: open.map { words[$0].end }.max() ?? 0),
322	                    previousEnd: before[first], nextStart: after[last + 1]))
323	            open = []
324	        }
325	        for (index, word) in words.enumerated() {
326	            guard word.filler else {
327	                close()
328	                continue
329	            }
330	            open.append(index)
331	        }
332	        close()
333	        return runs
334	    }

336	    private static func down(_ t: Ticks, _ grid: Ticks) -> Ticks {
337	        let q = t / grid
338	        return (t % grid != 0 && t < 0 ? q - 1 : q) * grid
339	    }
340	
341	    private static func up(_ t: Ticks, _ grid: Ticks) -> Ticks {
342	        let q = t / grid
343	        return (t % grid != 0 && t > 0 ? q + 1 : q) * grid
344	    }
345	
346	    /// A run's source span widened outward to the grid, bounded by its
347	    /// neighbours' grid points inward; nil when nothing is left.
348	    static func gridded(_ run: Run, grid: Ticks) -> SilenceDetector.Span? {
349	        guard grid > 0 else { return nil }
350	        let start = max(down(run.source.start, grid), up(run.previousEnd, grid))
351	        let end = min(up(run.source.end, grid), down(run.nextStart, grid))
352	        guard end > start else { return nil }
353	        return SilenceDetector.Span(start: start, end: end)
354	    }
355	
356	    /// A source span in project time, its start snapped up and its end down
357	    /// to the frame grid; nil when nothing is left.
358	    static func placed(
359	        _ source: SilenceDetector.Span, in job: Transcriber.Job, fps: Fps
360	    ) -> SilenceDetector.Span? {
361	        let span = SilenceDetector.Span(
362	            start: SilenceDetector.snapUpToFrame(
363	                MediaTranscript.project(source.start, in: job), fps: fps),
364	            end: SilenceDetector.snapDownToFrame(
365	                MediaTranscript.project(source.end, in: job), fps: fps))
366	        guard span.end > span.start else { return nil }
367	        return span
368	    }

370	    // MARK: - Detection
371	
372	    /// The candidates, what was dropped and why, and the merged ranges.
373	    static func detect(_ input: Input) -> Outcome {
374	        // Every neighbour's non-filler words in project time, read once.
375	        let guarded: [(clip: UInt32, words: [CaptionCues.Word])] = input.neighbours.map {
376	            ($0.job.clip,
377	             MediaTranscript.words(for: $0.job, in: $0.file).filter {
378	                 !FillerWords.isFiller($0.text)
379	             })
380	        }
381	        var candidates: [Candidate] = []
382	        var dropped: [Dropped] = []
383	        for clip in input.clips {
384	            let id = clip.job.clip
385	            for run in runs(of: clip.file, in: clip.job) {
386	                guard let source = gridded(run, grid: grid),
387	                    let span = placed(source, in: clip.job, fps: input.fps)
388	                else {
389	                    dropped.append(Dropped(clip: id, words: run.words, reason: .tooShort))
390	                    continue
391	                }
392	                if let reason = conflict(span, clip: id, guarded: guarded, input: input) {
393	                    dropped.append(Dropped(clip: id, words: run.words, reason: reason))
394	                    continue
395	                }
396	                candidates.append(Candidate(clip: id, words: run.words, source: source, span: span))
397	            }
398	        }
399	        return Outcome(
400	            spans: SilenceDetector.merged(candidates.map(\.span)), candidates: candidates,
401	            dropped: dropped, scope: input.scope,
402	            clips: Set(input.clips.map { $0.job.clip }).sorted(),
403	            needsTranscript: input.needsTranscript, skipped: input.skipped, locked: input.locked)
404	    }
405	
406	    /// Why a span may not be cut, in TR-9's order: another clip's word, a
407	    /// nest clip, a transition wall; nil when it may.
408	    private static func conflict(
409	        _ span: SilenceDetector.Span, clip: UInt32,
410	        guarded: [(clip: UInt32, words: [CaptionCues.Word])], input: Input
411	    ) -> DropReason? {
412	        for neighbour in guarded where neighbour.clip != clip {
413	            if let word = neighbour.words.first(where: {
414	                SilenceDetector.overlap(span, SilenceDetector.Span(start: $0.start, end: $0.end)) > 0
415	            }) {
416	                return .overlapsWord(clip: neighbour.clip, text: word.text)
417	            }
418	        }
419	        if let nest = input.nests.first(where: { SilenceDetector.overlap(span, $0.span) > 0 }) {
420	            return .nest(clip: nest.clip)
421	        }
422	        if input.walls.contains(where: { SilenceDetector.overlap(span, $0) > 0 }) {
423	            return .transition
424	        }
425	        return nil
426	    }
427	}

997	/// §11 TR-2, TR-7, TR-10): the request, the jobs and the estimate one press
998	/// of the sheet's Transcribe button sends for one media, shared by the sheet
999	/// (`FillerSheetController+Transcribe.swift`) and its mirror,
1000	/// `transcribe_for_fillers` (`AgentServer+Fillers.swift`), so the two cannot
1001	/// send different requests or quote different prices.
1002	///
1003	/// It holds no document. The jobs come from a snapshot and its media URLs,
1004	/// and the estimate from a cache directory, all passed by value — which is
1005	/// what lets the tool read them in one main-thread hop and run off main.
1006	///
1007	/// **TR-10's request.** The media's PREVIOUS request is kept — the marker's
1008	/// language, speaker labels and vocabulary — so the filler transcript is the
1009	/// same transcript as before with the fillers in it; the shipped models,
1010	/// `disfluencies: true` and `refresh: true` are added. With no marker it is
1011	/// detection, no speakers and no vocabulary. `refresh` is what makes a media
1012	/// whose caption transcript is current upload again: `CloudEstimate.fate`
1013	/// and `CloudTranscriber.transcribe` both judge currency for `.captions`,
1014	/// which ignores `disfluencies` (TR-2).
1015	enum FillerTranscription {
1016	
1017	    /// Always on: a media in the sheet's list has a transcript that serves
1018	    /// captions or none, and either way it must be fetched again.
1019	    static let refresh = true
1020	
1021	    /// The marker's request with fillers asked for, or detection with none.
1022	    static func options(for marker: TranscriptStamp?) -> TranscriptOptions {
1023	        TranscriptOptions(
1024	            speechModels: TranscriptOptions.shippedModels,
1025	            languageCode: marker?.languageCode,
1026	            speakerLabels: marker?.speakerLabels ?? false,
1027	            keytermsPrompt: marker?.keytermsPrompt ?? [],
1028	            disfluencies: true)
1029	    }
1030	
1031	    /// `Transcriber.jobs` over the snapshot's clips that play `media`; the
1032	    /// clips it refuses (a reversed one, one whose audio is off, a missing
1033	    /// file) are left out, as a caption run leaves them. `maps` are the
1034	    /// source maps of the snapshot's handle, so a ramped clip's job follows
1035	    /// its map (spec §11 SR-20 (d)).
1036	    static func jobs(
1037	        for media: UInt32, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, urls: [UInt32: URL], maps: SourceMaps
1038	    ) -> [Transcriber.Job] {
1039	        let clips = snapshot.clips.filter { clip in
1040	            guard case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source else { return false }
1041	            return id == media
1042	        }
1043	        return Transcriber.jobs(for: clips, in: snapshot, urls: urls, maps: maps).jobs
1044	    }
1045	
1046	    /// What one press would upload and cost, by `CloudEstimate`'s own rules
1047	    /// over the same request the run sends; nil when there is nothing to run.
1048	    static func estimate(
1049	        jobs: [Transcriber.Job], media: [UInt32: MediaSnapshot], cacheDirectory: URL
1050	    ) -> CloudEstimate? {
1051	        guard !jobs.isEmpty else { return nil }
1052	        let facts = CloudEstimate.facts(jobs: jobs, media: media, cacheDirectory: cacheDirectory)
1053	        return CloudEstimate(
1054	            facts: facts, options: options(for: facts.first?.marker), refresh: refresh)
1055	    }

---
title: "What counts as silent"
description: "How Remove Silences decides a moment is quiet: Voice or Level, what the mix changes, and why a stretch isn't proposed."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Remove Silences cuts a stretch only when it's quiet as you hear it, in the mix, and only where every clip in scope is quiet at once. **Judge by:** in the sheet picks how each moment is tested.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Silences…"
  where="Judge by: in the Remove Silences sheet"
  tools="detect_silence"
  needs="Nothing. Voice detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Judge by Voice or Level

| **Judge by:** | A moment is quiet when |
| --- | --- |
| **Voice** | Nobody is talking. |
| **Level** | The sound in the mix is at or below the threshold. |

The sheet opens on **Voice** every time, unless [the voice model can't be used](#when-the-voice-model-cant-be-used).

Voice listens for speech, not for loudness. In a clip that holds a voice, a loud sound that isn't speech still counts as quiet. If a recording has sounds you want to keep, such as the audio of a demo, choose **Level**.

## Voice mode

A voice-activity model that comes with Frame Job scores every 32 ms of a file for speech, and a moment counts as speech when its score reaches the voice confidence. The sheet always uses 0.5. A quiet microphone isn't mistaken for silence, and a hum isn't mistaken for speech.

You don't start the analysis. It runs by itself after you import a file or open a project, listens to each file once and keeps the answer with the project. It runs on your Mac, and nothing is uploaded.

In Voice mode the threshold row reads **Level if no voice:**, and it does two jobs:

- It's the level for [clips with no voice in them](#clips-with-no-voice-are-judged-by-level).
- A clip the mix turns down to that level or lower is quiet whatever it holds. At the default −40 dBFS, that's a clip turned down by 40 dB or more.

The same voice analysis also serves [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/), [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/), [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/), [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/), [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) and the [transcript's word timing](/captions/transcript-words/).

## Clips with no voice are judged by level

In Voice mode, a clip with no voice in it at all, such as music or a tone, would read as quiet from start to end. So Frame Job judges that clip by level instead, against **Level if no voice:**, and the sheet names it:

- One clip: "Intro music at 00:00:12:00 holds no voice and is judged by level."
- Several: "3 clips hold no voice and are judged by level: …", followed by each clip's name and time.

The test covers only the part of the file the clip plays. That's why the sheet names clips and not files: two clips of one file can be judged differently.

## Level mode

In Level mode a moment is quiet when the sound in the mix is at or below **Quieter than:**. That's the file's waveform with the [mix](#silence-is-measured-in-the-mix) applied, measured in 10 ms steps. When a step holds more than one reading, as it does in a clip playing at ×2, the louder reading counts, so the test can only keep more.

**Quieter than:** runs from −80 to −10 dBFS and starts at −40 dBFS. See [The controls](/cleanup/remove-silences/#the-controls).

## Silence is measured in the mix

Remove Silences measures what you hear, not the raw file. These all count:

- The clip's volume, its fades and any volume change in an action
- Ducking from another clip
- Muting a clip or a track, and soloing another track
- The track's volume

In Level mode, a clip you've turned down reads quieter by exactly as much. In Voice mode, turning a clip down makes it quiet only once it reaches the level in **Level if no voice:**. Above that, speech is still speech.

Effects on the clip don't count. Remove Silences hears the file without its [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) or [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/).

## Every clip in scope has to be quiet

A stretch is silent only where every clip in scope is quiet. A music bed under a voice-over therefore keeps the pauses in the speech from being cut, because the music is still playing through them.

To cut those pauses, select the voice clip and set **In:** to **Selected clips**, so only the voice is measured.

:::caution
The scope changes what's measured, not what's cut. The cut still runs across every unlocked track, so the music is cut at the same places. [Lock its track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#lock-track) to leave the music where it is. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).
:::

## Muted clips are left out

A clip the mix silences all the way through is left out of the analysis entirely. That covers a muted clip, a clip silenced by a solo, and a clip turned down or faded to nothing. This holds in both scopes, even for a selected clip.

So a muted music bed is never read as one long silence covering the whole song. It doesn't hold a cut up either. Where it's the only thing playing, there's nothing to measure, and the stretch is left alone like a gap.

## While a file is still being analysed

Nothing inside a file is proposed until its analysis is ready, so a clip can't be cut as silence because its waveform hasn't arrived yet. This often shows straight after an import.

| Mode | What it waits for | The sheet says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level | The waveform | "The waveform is still being analysed for …" |
| Voice | The voice analysis | "Speech is still being analysed for …" |
| Voice, for a clip with no voice | The voice analysis, then the waveform | "The waveform is still being analysed for … Anything inside it that holds no voice is left alone until it lands." |

There's one exception in every mode. A part the mix has already turned down far enough to be quiet can still be proposed, because no analysis can change that answer, and the sheet names the clip.

Leave the sheet open if you like. It updates as each file lands.

If a file's sound can't be read to its end, Frame Job doesn't keep the analysis, and it tries again the next time you open the project. Until then, nothing inside that file is proposed.

## When the voice model can't be used

If the voice model can't be used on this Mac, the sheet opens in **Level** mode with **Voice** greyed out, and it says "The voice model could not be used, so quiet is judged by level." This lasts until you relaunch Frame Job.

## Limits of Voice mode

- It can miss a soft first word in a quiet recording. Raise **Keep at ends:** if a word gets clipped.
- Singing and voice-like instruments may read as speech.
- A clip that holds any voice is judged by voice for its whole length. So a long music clip with a little speech in it isn't judged by level, and the music around that speech reads as quiet. Use **In:** **Selected clips** to keep it out of the measurement.
- The model hears each file mixed down to mono, so a voice on one side of a stereo recording sounds quieter to it.

## With an agent

`detect_silence` takes the same choices as the sheet, and one the sheet doesn't have: the voice confidence, which is how sure the model must be for a moment to count as speech. It runs from 0.1 to 0.9, with a default of 0.5, and it also decides which clips count as holding no voice. It works in Voice mode only. Frame Job turns it down in Level mode or outside that range, and says why.

While the voice model can't be used, an agent that asks for Voice by name is turned down. One that doesn't name a mode gets Level, with the same note the sheet shows. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).

## Related

- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/)
- [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/)
- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
- [Ducking](/audio/ducking/)

---
title: "Remove Filler Words"
description: "Find the ums and uhs in your speech, see what would go, and cut them all as one edit."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Remove Filler Words finds the ums and uhs in your speech, shows you what it would cut, and takes them out on the words' own timings, as one undo step. There's nothing to tune.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…"
  tools={['detect_fillers', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript']}
  needs="An AssemblyAI key, unless a file in scope already has a transcript made with filler words."
/>

## Remove the filler words

<Steps>

1. If you only want some clips read, select them. See [Which clips are read](#which-clips-are-read).

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. It's after **Remove Silences…** and has no keyboard shortcut.

3. If the sheet lists files with no filler transcript yet, press **Transcribe** beside each one you want read. This uploads the file's audio to AssemblyAI and costs money, so the sheet shows the estimate first. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/).

4. Check what's shaded on the timeline, and read the count in the sheet, such as "3 cuts · removes 00:00:01:12".

5. Choose **Remove**.

</Steps>

**Remove** is off when there's nothing to cut, when the sheet reads "No cuts", and while a transcription is running. One <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> puts everything back, because the whole cut is a single **Remove Filler Words** undo step.

The command is on when the timeline has a clip that plays sound from a media file, forwards, with its sound on, and you've either set an AssemblyAI key or a file in scope already has a transcript made with filler words. With neither, it's greyed and reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).

## Which words are fillers

A word counts as a filler when it's on this fixed list, ignoring capitals and any punctuation at its ends:

um · uh · hmm · mhm · uh-huh · ah · huh · hm · m · er · erm

"Uh huh" written as two words matches as two fillers, and "uh-huh" matches as one.

:::caution
The list can't be changed, and the sheet can't keep a single filler. A real "ah" or "er", or the letter "M" said aloud, is treated as a filler too, so check the shading before you choose **Remove**.
:::

## Which clips are read

Remove Filler Words reads the selected clips when the selection includes speech from a media file, and the sheet then says "Only the selected clips are read." Otherwise it reads every clip. There's no scope menu in the sheet, so make the selection first.

Some clips can't be read:

| Clip | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| It's on a locked track | Its fillers aren't read, because the cut can neither cut nor move it. The sheet counts them: "1 clip is on a locked track, which the cut neither cuts nor moves, so its fillers were not read." |
| It plays in reverse, its sound is switched off, its file is missing, or its file has no audio track | It has no words to read, and it's passed over without a note. |
| It's a [nest](/editing/nests/) | The words inside a nest aren't read from outside it. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and run the command there, where it works on the nest's own timeline. |

When nothing in scope has words to read, the sheet says "Nothing in scope plays speech from a media file, so nothing was read."

## What gets cut

Each run of consecutive fillers becomes one cut. A run ends at the next real word, so two fillers with a pause between them and no word go together, pause included. The pauses before and after a run stay. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) takes those out.

The cut is placed to take the whole filler and nothing else:

- It widens outward to a 32 ms speech grid, so all of the filler goes, but it never reaches into the words on either side.
- Its edges then snap inward to the frame grid, as Remove Silences' do. Up to a frame of the filler can remain at each end.

Cuts that touch or overlap join into one, and the count in the sheet is of the joined cuts.

After that it's a normal clean-up cut. It runs across every unlocked track, closes the timeline over each cut, and markers keep their place. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).

## Fillers left in whole

A filler is never trimmed. Frame Job leaves the whole run in when:

- It's too short to cut. A tiny filler can end up with nothing left once it's on both grids.
- Cutting it would reach a word spoken in another clip on any unlocked track, whether or not that clip is in scope. The cut ripples every unlocked track, so it would take that word with it.
- Cutting it would reach a nest clip on an unlocked track.
- Cutting it would reach a transition on an unlocked track, or the area around one.

The sheet counts these, one for each run: "2 fillers are left in: too short to cut, or cutting would reach another clip's word, a nest or a transition."

## Good to know

- **Protection needs a transcript.** A cut is kept away from speech in another clip only when that clip's file has a saved AssemblyAI transcript, made with or without filler words. Speech on another unlocked track with no such transcript isn't protected, so check the shading there.
- **The service can miss a filler.** A filler AssemblyAI doesn't return isn't cut. One it returns that isn't on the list stays in, both in the cut and in your captions.
- **A filler belongs to the clip it starts in.** It's read when it starts inside the part of the file the clip plays.

## With an agent

`detect_fillers` reads the same ranges the sheet would cut and changes nothing. Pass them to `ripple_delete_ranges` to make the cut. Any cut made this way is one undo step called **Ripple Delete**, not **Remove Filler Words**.

- An agent can name the clips to read. Left to itself, it follows the same selection rule as the sheet.
- `detect_fillers` only reads transcripts that are already saved, so it needs no key and never uses the network. It names the files that have none.
- `transcribe_for_fillers` makes a transcript for one of those files. It's a paid upload, and the built-in assistant can't use it, so press **Transcribe** in the sheet yourself.
- Where the sheet counts, an agent gets detail: every run that's left in with its own reason, and every named clip it couldn't read.
- `get_transcript` and `get_timeline_transcript` mark each word that's on the [filler list](#which-words-are-fillers).

See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).

## Related

- [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/)
- [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/)
- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/)
- [Cut false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/)
- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/)

The list can't be changed, and the sheet can't keep a single filler. A real "ah" or "er", or the letter "M" said aloud, is treated as a filler too, so check the shading before you choose **Remove**.
:::

## Which clips are read

Remove Filler Words reads the selected clips when the selection includes speech from a media file, and the sheet then says "Only the selected clips are read." Otherwise it reads every clip. There's no scope menu in the sheet, so make the selection first.

Some clips can't be read:

| Clip | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| It's on a locked track | Its fillers aren't read, because the cut can neither cut nor move it. The sheet counts them: "1 clip is on a locked track, which the cut neither cuts nor moves, so its fillers were not read." |
| It plays in reverse, its sound is switched off, its file is missing, or its file has no audio track | It has no words to read, and it's passed over without a note. |
| It's a [nest](/editing/nests/) | The words inside a nest aren't read from outside it. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and run the command there, where it works on the nest's own timeline. |

When nothing in scope has words to read, the sheet says "Nothing in scope plays speech from a media file, so nothing was read."

## What gets cut

Each run of consecutive fillers becomes one cut. A run ends at the next real word, so two fillers with a pause between them and no word go together, pause included. The pauses before and after a run stay. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) takes those out.

The cut is placed to take the whole filler and nothing else:

- It widens outward to a 32 ms speech grid, so all of the filler goes, but it never reaches into the words on either side.
- Its edges then snap inward to the frame grid, as Remove Silences' do. Up to a frame of the filler can remain at each end.

Cuts that touch or overlap join into one, and the count in the sheet is of the joined cuts.

After that it's a normal clean-up cut. It runs across every unlocked track, closes the timeline over each cut, and markers keep their place. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).

## Fillers left in whole

A filler is never trimmed. Frame Job leaves the whole run in when:

- It's too short to cut. A tiny filler can end up with nothing left once it's on both grids.
- Cutting it would reach a word spoken in another clip on any unlocked track, whether or not that clip is in scope. The cut ripples every unlocked track, so it would take that word with it.
- Cutting it would reach a nest clip on an unlocked track.
- Cutting it would reach a transition on an unlocked track, or the area around one.

The sheet counts these, one for each run: "2 fillers are left in: too short to cut, or cutting would reach another clip's word, a nest or a transition."

## Good to know

- **Protection needs a transcript.** A cut is kept away from speech in another clip only when that clip's file has a saved AssemblyAI transcript, made with or without filler words. Speech on another unlocked track with no such transcript isn't protected, so check the shading there.
- **The service can miss a filler.** A filler AssemblyAI doesn't return isn't cut. One it returns that isn't on the list stays in, both in the cut and in your captions.
- **A filler belongs to the clip it starts in.** It's read when it starts inside the part of the file the clip plays.

## With an agent

`detect_fillers` reads the same ranges the sheet would cut and changes nothing. Pass them to `ripple_delete_ranges` to make the cut. Any cut made this way is one undo step called **Ripple Delete**, not **Remove Filler Words**.

- An agent can name the clips to read. Left to itself, it follows the same selection rule as the sheet.
- `detect_fillers` only reads transcripts that are already saved, so it needs no key and never uses the network. It names the files that have none.
- `transcribe_for_fillers` makes a transcript for one of those files. It's a paid upload, and the built-in assistant can't use it, so press **Transcribe** in the sheet yourself.
- Where the sheet counts, an agent gets detail: every run that's left in with its own reason, and every named clip it couldn't read.
- `get_transcript` and `get_timeline_transcript` mark each word that's on the [filler list](#which-words-are-fillers).

See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).

## Related

- [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/)
- [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/)
- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/)
- [Cut false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/)
- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

---
title: "What counts as silent"
description: "How Remove Silences decides a moment is quiet: Voice or Level, what the mix changes, and why a stretch isn't proposed."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Remove Silences cuts a stretch only when it's quiet as you hear it, in the mix, and only where every clip in scope is quiet at once. **Judge by:** in the sheet picks how each moment is tested.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Silences…"
  where="Judge by: in the Remove Silences sheet"
  tools="detect_silence"
  needs="Nothing. Voice detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Judge by Voice or Level

| **Judge by:** | A moment is quiet when |
| --- | --- |
| **Voice** | Nobody is talking. |
| **Level** | The sound in the mix is at or below the threshold. |

The sheet opens on **Voice** every time, unless [the voice model can't be used](#when-the-voice-model-cant-be-used).

Voice listens for speech, not for loudness. In a clip that holds a voice, a loud sound that isn't speech still counts as quiet. If a recording has sounds you want to keep, such as the audio of a demo, choose **Level**.

## Voice mode

A voice-activity model that comes with Frame Job scores every 32 ms of a file for speech, and a moment counts as speech when its score reaches the voice confidence. The sheet always uses 0.5. A quiet microphone isn't mistaken for silence, and a hum isn't mistaken for speech.

You don't start the analysis. It runs by itself after you import a file or open a project, listens to each file once and keeps the answer with the project. It runs on your Mac, and nothing is uploaded.

In Voice mode the threshold row reads **Level if no voice:**, and it does two jobs:

- It's the level for [clips with no voice in them](#clips-with-no-voice-are-judged-by-level).
- A clip the mix turns down to that level or lower is quiet whatever it holds. At the default −40 dBFS, that's a clip turned down by 40 dB or more.

The same voice analysis also serves [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/), [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/), [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/), [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/), [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) and the [transcript's word timing](/captions/transcript-words/).

## Clips with no voice are judged by level

In Voice mode, a clip with no voice in it at all, such as music or a tone, would read as quiet from start to end. So Frame Job judges that clip by level instead, against **Level if no voice:**, and the sheet names it:

- One clip: "Intro music at 00:00:12:00 holds no voice and is judged by level."
- Several: "3 clips hold no voice and are judged by level: …", followed by each clip's name and time.

The test covers only the part of the file the clip plays. That's why the sheet names clips and not files: two clips of one file can be judged differently.

## Level mode

In Level mode a moment is quiet when the sound in the mix is at or below **Quieter than:**. That's the file's waveform with the [mix](#silence-is-measured-in-the-mix) applied, measured in 10 ms steps. When a step holds more than one reading, as it does in a clip playing at ×2, the louder reading counts, so the test can only keep more.

**Quieter than:** runs from −80 to −10 dBFS and starts at −40 dBFS. See [The controls](/cleanup/remove-silences/#the-controls).

## Silence is measured in the mix

Remove Silences measures what you hear, not the raw file. These all count:

- The clip's volume, its fades and any volume change in an action
- Ducking from another clip
- Muting a clip or a track, and soloing another track
- The track's volume

In Level mode, a clip you've turned down reads quieter by exactly as much. In Voice mode, turning a clip down makes it quiet only once it reaches the level in **Level if no voice:**. Above that, speech is still speech.

Effects on the clip don't count. Remove Silences hears the file without its [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) or [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/).

## Every clip in scope has to be quiet

A stretch is silent only where every clip in scope is quiet. A music bed under a voice-over therefore keeps the pauses in the speech from being cut, because the music is still playing through them.

To cut those pauses, select the voice clip and set **In:** to **Selected clips**, so only the voice is measured.

:::caution
The scope changes what's measured, not what's cut. The cut still runs across every unlocked track, so the music is cut at the same places. [Lock its track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#lock-track) to leave the music where it is. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).
:::

## Muted clips are left out

A clip the mix silences all the way through is left out of the analysis entirely. That covers a muted clip, a clip silenced by a solo, and a clip turned down or faded to nothing. This holds in both scopes, even for a selected clip.

So a muted music bed is never read as one long silence covering the whole song. It doesn't hold a cut up either. Where it's the only thing playing, there's nothing to measure, and the stretch is left alone like a gap.

## While a file is still being analysed

Nothing inside a file is proposed until its analysis is ready, so a clip can't be cut as silence because its waveform hasn't arrived yet. This often shows straight after an import.

| Mode | What it waits for | The sheet says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level | The waveform | "The waveform is still being analysed for …" |
| Voice | The voice analysis | "Speech is still being analysed for …" |
| Voice, for a clip with no voice | The voice analysis, then the waveform | "The waveform is still being analysed for … Anything inside it that holds no voice is left alone until it lands." |

There's one exception in every mode. A part the mix has already turned down far enough to be quiet can still be proposed, because no analysis can change that answer, and the sheet names the clip.

Leave the sheet open if you like. It updates as each file lands.

If a file's sound can't be read to its end, Frame Job doesn't keep the analysis, and it tries again the next time you open the project. Until then, nothing inside that file is proposed.

## When the voice model can't be used

If the voice model can't be used on this Mac, the sheet opens in **Level** mode with **Voice** greyed out, and it says "The voice model could not be used, so quiet is judged by level." This lasts until you relaunch Frame Job.

## Limits of Voice mode

- It can miss a soft first word in a quiet recording. Raise **Keep at ends:** if a word gets clipped.
- Singing and voice-like instruments may read as speech.
- A clip that holds any voice is judged by voice for its whole length. So a long music clip with a little speech in it isn't judged by level, and the music around that speech reads as quiet. Use **In:** **Selected clips** to keep it out of the measurement.
- The model hears each file mixed down to mono, so a voice on one side of a stereo recording sounds quieter to it.

## With an agent

`detect_silence` takes the same choices as the sheet, and one the sheet doesn't have: the voice confidence, which is how sure the model must be for a moment to count as speech. It runs from 0.1 to 0.9, with a default of 0.5, and it also decides which clips count as holding no voice. It works in Voice mode only. Frame Job turns it down in Level mode or outside that range, and says why.

While the voice model can't be used, an agent that asks for Voice by name is turned down. One that doesn't name a mode gets Level, with the same note the sheet shows. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).

## Related

- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/)
- [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/)
- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
- [Ducking](/audio/ducking/)

---
title: "Remove Filler Words"
description: "Find the ums and uhs in your speech, see what would go, and cut them all as one edit."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Remove Filler Words finds the ums and uhs in your speech, shows you what it would cut, and takes them out on the words' own timings, as one undo step. There's nothing to tune.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…"
  tools={['detect_fillers', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript']}
  needs="An AssemblyAI key, unless a file in scope already has a transcript made with filler words."
/>

## Remove the filler words

<Steps>

1. If you only want some clips read, select them. See [Which clips are read](#which-clips-are-read).

2. Choose **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. It's after **Remove Silences…** and has no keyboard shortcut.

3. If the sheet lists files with no filler transcript yet, press **Transcribe** beside each one you want read. This uploads the file's audio to AssemblyAI and costs money, so the sheet shows the estimate first. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/).

4. Check what's shaded on the timeline, and read the count in the sheet, such as "3 cuts · removes 00:00:01:12".

5. Choose **Remove**.

</Steps>

**Remove** is off when there's nothing to cut, when the sheet reads "No cuts", and while a transcription is running. One <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> puts everything back, because the whole cut is a single **Remove Filler Words** undo step.

The command is on when the timeline has a clip that plays sound from a media file, forwards, with its sound on, and you've either set an AssemblyAI key or a file in scope already has a transcript made with filler words. With neither, it's greyed and reads **Remove Filler Words… (needs your AssemblyAI key)**. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).

## Which words are fillers

A word counts as a filler when it's on this fixed list, ignoring capitals and any punctuation at its ends:

um · uh · hmm · mhm · uh-huh · ah · huh · hm · m · er · erm

"Uh huh" written as two words matches as two fillers, and "uh-huh" matches as one.

:::caution
The list can't be changed, and the sheet can't keep a single filler. A real "ah" or "er", or the letter "M" said aloud, is treated as a filler too, so check the shading before you choose **Remove**.
:::

## Which clips are read

Remove Filler Words reads the selected clips when the selection includes speech from a media file, and the sheet then says "Only the selected clips are read." Otherwise it reads every clip. There's no scope menu in the sheet, so make the selection first.

Some clips can't be read:

| Clip | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| It's on a locked track | Its fillers aren't read, because the cut can neither cut nor move it. The sheet counts them: "1 clip is on a locked track, which the cut neither cuts nor moves, so its fillers were not read." |
| It plays in reverse, its sound is switched off, its file is missing, or its file has no audio track | It has no words to read, and it's passed over without a note. |
| It's a [nest](/editing/nests/) | The words inside a nest aren't read from outside it. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and run the command there, where it works on the nest's own timeline. |

When nothing in scope has words to read, the sheet says "Nothing in scope plays speech from a media file, so nothing was read."

## What gets cut

Each run of consecutive fillers becomes one cut. A run ends at the next real word, so two fillers with a pause between them and no word go together, pause included. The pauses before and after a run stay. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) takes those out.

The cut is placed to take the whole filler and nothing else:

- It widens outward to a 32 ms speech grid, so all of the filler goes, but it never reaches into the words on either side.
- Its edges then snap inward to the frame grid, as Remove Silences' do. Up to a frame of the filler can remain at each end.

Cuts that touch or overlap join into one, and the count in the sheet is of the joined cuts.

After that it's a normal clean-up cut. It runs across every unlocked track, closes the timeline over each cut, and markers keep their place. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).

## Fillers left in whole

A filler is never trimmed. Frame Job leaves the whole run in when:

- It's too short to cut. A tiny filler can end up with nothing left once it's on both grids.
- Cutting it would reach a word spoken in another clip on any unlocked track, whether or not that clip is in scope. The cut ripples every unlocked track, so it would take that word with it.
- Cutting it would reach a nest clip on an unlocked track.
- Cutting it would reach a transition on an unlocked track, or the area around one.

The sheet counts these, one for each run: "2 fillers are left in: too short to cut, or cutting would reach another clip's word, a nest or a transition."

## Good to know

- **Protection needs a transcript.** A cut is kept away from speech in another clip only when that clip's file has a saved AssemblyAI transcript, made with or without filler words. Speech on another unlocked track with no such transcript isn't protected, so check the shading there.
- **The service can miss a filler.** A filler AssemblyAI doesn't return isn't cut. One it returns that isn't on the list stays in, both in the cut and in your captions.
- **A filler belongs to the clip it starts in.** It's read when it starts inside the part of the file the clip plays.

## With an agent

`detect_fillers` reads the same ranges the sheet would cut and changes nothing. Pass them to `ripple_delete_ranges` to make the cut. Any cut made this way is one undo step called **Ripple Delete**, not **Remove Filler Words**.

- An agent can name the clips to read. Left to itself, it follows the same selection rule as the sheet.
- `detect_fillers` only reads transcripts that are already saved, so it needs no key and never uses the network. It names the files that have none.
- `transcribe_for_fillers` makes a transcript for one of those files. It's a paid upload, and the built-in assistant can't use it, so press **Transcribe** in the sheet yourself.
- Where the sheet counts, an agent gets detail: every run that's left in with its own reason, and every named clip it couldn't read.
- `get_transcript` and `get_timeline_transcript` mark each word that's on the [filler list](#which-words-are-fillers).

See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).

## Related

- [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/)
- [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/)
- [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/)
- [Cut false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/)
- [Cut by deleting words](/captions/delete-words/)
